question: A function \(f\) is defined recursively by \(f(1)=f(2)=1\) and \[ f(n)=f(n-1)-f(n-2)+n \] for all integers \(n\ge3.\) What is \(f(2018)?\)
solution:
Substituting the recurrence into itself cancels neighboring terms, letting us move several indices at once. For \(n\ge4\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n)&=f(n-1)-f(n-2)+n\\
&=[f(n-2)-f(n-3)+(n-1)]-f(n-2)+n\\
&=-f(n-3)+2n-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(n\ge7\), apply this same identity to \(f(n-3)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n)&=-[-f(n-6)+2(n-3)-1]+2n-1\\
&=f(n-6)+6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the terms with indices \(2,8,14,\ldots\) form an arithmetic sequence, increasing by \(6\) each time. Since \(2018=2+6\cdot336\),
\[
f(2018)=f(2)+6\cdot336=1+2016=\boxed{2017}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{B}\).
